accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal, established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, started functioning in:
accepted.x: The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October 2010 and began functioning in July 2011.
accepted.tq: Separate the establishment date from the date on which the institution began functioning.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated purpose of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Relief and compensation for environmental damage
Conservation of forests and natural resources
Conducting elections to local bodies in environmentally sensitive areas
accepted.x: The NGT deals with environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental legal rights, and relief and compensation for damage. Conducting local-body elections is not its function.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the tribunal’s stated environmental jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal:
1. It is a statutory body and not a constitutional body.
2. Its legal basis is connected with the right to a healthy environment under Article 21.
3. It is bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The NGT is a statutory body whose purpose is linked to the Article 21 right to a healthy environment. It is not bound by the CPC, though it is guided by natural justice.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed procedural statement about the CPC.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the principal and zonal benches of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Principal Bench—New Delhi; Zonal Benches—Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai
Principal Bench—Mumbai; Zonal Benches—Delhi, Jaipur, Patna and Kochi
Principal Bench—New Delhi; Zonal Benches—Shimla, Shillong and Jodhpur
Principal Bench—Bhopal; Zonal Benches—Pune, Chennai, Lucknow and Ranchi
accepted.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi, while the Zonal Benches are at Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure location of the Principal Bench and distinguish zonal from circuit benches.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of Bench)
A. Principal Bench
B. Zonal Bench
C. Circuit Bench

List-II (Location)
1. New Delhi
2. Pune
3. Shimla

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi, Pune is a Zonal Bench, and Shimla is a Circuit Bench.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive bench-location pair first, then eliminate codes that interchange zonal and circuit benches.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a Circuit Bench of the National Green Tribunal?
accepted.x: The Circuit Benches are located at Shimla, Shillong and Jodhpur. Kolkata, Chennai and Pune are Zonal Bench locations.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely related zonal and circuit bench lists.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The composition of the National Green Tribunal includes:
o: A Chairperson and members drawn exclusively from the scientific community
A Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members
Only serving Supreme Court judges and representatives of State Pollution Control Boards
A Governor, Chief Minister and district collectors
accepted.x: The NGT consists of a Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory composition by separating judicial and expert components.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. The Chairperson may be a retired Supreme Court judge.
2. The Chairperson may be a Chief Justice of a High Court.
3. Justice Prakash Shrivastava was the Chairperson as on 15 January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Chairperson can be a retired Supreme Court judge or a Chief Justice of a High Court. Justice Prakash Shrivastava held the position as on 15 January 2026.
accepted.tq: Combine eligibility conditions with the current office-holder without confusing judicial categories.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The number of Judicial Members and Expert Members in the National Green Tribunal is stated to be:
accepted.x: The composition provision referred to here specifies 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct numerical range rather than relying on the tribunal’s total membership.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Applications before the National Green Tribunal are required to be disposed of within:
accepted.x: The prescribed period for disposal of applications by the NGT is six months.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the application-disposal period from the appeal period.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - establishment, purpose, seat, benches, composition, chair  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following environmental matters has been included among the NGT’s directions or docket matters?
accepted.x: NGT directions and matters include Ganga pollution control, waste management, industrial monitoring, and cases such as the Dhanauri wetland and Saparnika river matters.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed activity belongs to the tribunal’s environmental docket.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The time limit prescribed in the August 2023 direction for the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees was:
accepted.x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.
accepted.tq: Separate the quantity of the direction from its compliance period.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In 2022, the National Green Tribunal imposed fines on states in connection with waste mismanagement. Which pair was specifically associated with such fines?
accepted.x: Maharashtra and West Bengal were cited as examples of states fined by the NGT for waste mismanagement in 2022.
accepted.tq: Match the environmental violation with the correctly associated states.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NGT action concerning the LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam?
o: It transferred the matter to the National Environment Appellate Authority without any financial direction.
It took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
It ordered a permanent ban on all chemical industries in Andhra Pradesh.
It directed the Border Roads Organisation to undertake plantation in Uttarakhand.
accepted.x: Following the Visakhapatnam styrene leak in May 2020, the NGT took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the authority’s action to the correct incident instead of confusing separate NGT orders.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Nicobar project—High-Powered Committee on NGT directions
Sewage in drinking water—suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Styrene leak—Maharashtra and West Bengal waste-management fines
accepted.x: The styrene leak concerned LG Polymers at Visakhapatnam and led to an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore. Maharashtra and West Bengal were associated with fines for waste mismanagement.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped incident-and-state pairing.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The High-Powered Committee relating to the Great Nicobar project was set up pursuant to directions of the:
accepted.x: A High-Powered Committee was set up on the directions of the National Green Tribunal in relation to the Great Nicobar project.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who directed the committee’ approach to distinguish environmental institutions.
accepted.sec: Landmark NGT orders - mining bans, plantation/penalty directions, fines on states, AP cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following Acts falls OUTSIDE the National Green Tribunal’s Schedule I jurisdiction?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
accepted.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is outside the listed Schedule I Acts of the NGT. The Air Act, Biological Diversity Act and Public Liability Insurance Act are included.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded statute from a list of closely related environmental laws.
accepted.sec: NGT powers - Acts, principles, appeal, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
3. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
4. Forest Rights Act, 2006
Which of the above are included among the Acts under which the NGT hears cases?
accepted.x: The Water Act, Forest (Conservation) Act and Environment (Protection) Act are included. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is outside the NGT’s Schedule I list.
accepted.tq: Separate the included environmental statutes from the specifically excluded Forest Rights Act.
accepted.sec: NGT powers - Acts, principles, appeal, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which set contains the principles that the National Green Tribunal is required to apply?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter pays principle
Natural resources doctrine, parliamentary privilege and eminent domain
User pays, caveat emptor and laissez-faire
Absolute liability, federal supremacy and electoral accountability
accepted.x: The NGT applies sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
accepted.tq: Recognise the standard trio of environmental adjudicatory principles.
accepted.sec: NGT powers - Acts, principles, appeal, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: An aggrieved person seeking to challenge an order of the National Green Tribunal must approach the Supreme Court within:
accepted.x: An appeal against an NGT order lies to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Supreme Court appeal period from the NGT’s six-month disposal period.
accepted.sec: NGT powers - Acts, principles, appeal, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: NGT is a quasi-judicial tribunal, whereas CPCB is a statutory regulator.
NGT functions under the Water Act alone, whereas CPCB functions under the NGT Act.
NGT sets pollution standards, whereas CPCB awards compensation.
Both are constitutional bodies with identical adjudicatory powers.
accepted.x: The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation under the NGT Act. The CPCB is a statutory regulator under the Water Act and Air Act that sets standards, monitors and advises the Centre.
accepted.tq: Compare the institution’s legal character and core function rather than its common environmental field.
accepted.sec: NGT powers - Acts, principles, appeal, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was distinctive because it provided for:
o: Strict liability for accidents involving hazardous substances
Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
accepted.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.
accepted.tq: Associate the predecessor law with its distinctive liability principle.
accepted.sec: Predecessor tribunals - NET Act and NEAA Act  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995:
1. It was never made operational.
2. It was repealed by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
3. It dealt with strict liability for hazardous-substance accidents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Act was never operationalised, was repealed by the NGT Act, and provided for strict liability in hazardous-substance accidents.
accepted.tq: Test the predecessor law through its year, fate and substantive legal principle.
accepted.sec: Predecessor tribunals - NET Act and NEAA Act  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 primarily provided for hearing appeals against:
accepted.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority heard appeals against environmental clearances.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the appellate authority’s subject matter from the NGT’s wider jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Predecessor tribunals - NET Act and NEAA Act  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Environment Appellate Authority is correct?
o: It was dissolved and its Act was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
It became a constitutional court under Article 21.
It was established under the NGT Act, 2010 and continues to function independently.
It was converted into the Central Pollution Control Board.
accepted.x: The NEAA was dissolved, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
accepted.tq: Use the fate of the predecessor institution to reject continuation and conversion traps.
accepted.sec: Predecessor tribunals - NET Act and NEAA Act  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The inter-state dispute concerning the Polavaram project primarily relates to submergence in:
accepted.x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the neighbouring states directly affected by the project’s submergence issue.
accepted.sec: Clearance and inter-state disputes over AP projects - Polavaram, Amaravati  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A proposal submitted for environmental appraisal through PARIVESH is automatically transferred when the State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to appraise it within:
accepted.x: Under the stated 2026 arrangement, a proposal is auto-transferred through PARIVESH if the SEAC does not appraise it within 120 days.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise trigger period for automatic transfer in the clearance process.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PARIVESH is best described as a:
o: Single-window portal for environmental and related clearances
Scientific body that prepares only climate reports
accepted.x: PARIVESH functions as a single-window portal for clearances and has been upgraded to PARIVESH 3.0 using artificial intelligence.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional role from the service it provides rather than its environmental subject area.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PARIVESH 3.0 is associated with the use of:
o: Artificial intelligence in the clearance portal
Satellite launch technology for biodiversity mapping
accepted.x: PARIVESH 3.0 uses artificial intelligence as part of the upgraded single-window clearance system.
accepted.tq: Match the technology with the correct environmental-governance platform.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the backup arrangement referred to for environmental appraisal bodies in 2026?
o: NGT for SEIAA and NEAA for SEAC
SCEIA for SEIAA and SAEIA for SEAC
EAC for SEIAA and CPCB for SEAC
SAEIA for SEIAA and SCEIA for SEAC
accepted.x: The stated backup bodies are SAEIA in place of SEIAA and SCEIA in place of SEAC.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similar abbreviations by matching each backup body to its parent body.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the stated revised arrangements, the tenure of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC members is:
o: Four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70
Five years, with unlimited terms and no age limit
Three years, with one renewal and a maximum age of 65
accepted.x: The tenure was raised to four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70 years for members of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC.
accepted.tq: Combine tenure, term limit and age limit to avoid selecting a partly correct option.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The maximum tenure of the SAEIA and SCEIA arrangement, including the stated extension, is:
accepted.x: The tenure is stated as six months plus another six months, subject to a maximum of one year.
accepted.tq: Add the base tenure and extension while observing the explicit maximum limit.
accepted.sec: Clearance bodies - EAC, SEIAA, PARIVESH  [GROUP-II]
